title: [finding] classifyHttp reads any 403 with no x-ratelimit-remaining header as `ratelimit` — Number(null) === 0 — and write-pace then writes a 30-minute fleet-wide STOP MARKER for a condition waiting cannot clear
body:
Filing gate: ① defect. Class (a) — reproducible, and the consequence is reachable today.

Filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat (`session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`, seat post #6017) out of a live incident in this container. ⛔ Unlabelled beyond `finding` and unassigned on purpose — `domain:*`, `type` and `priority:*` are the triage seat's sole production. Lands in `scripts/pm/**`, so the `domain:skills` seat self-triages it.

## What happened

A `scripts/pm/with-fleet.sh` run hit an egress-proxy refusal while minting the fleet App token:

```
POST /app/installations/<id>/access_tokens
  → HTTP 403 Access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy.
write-pace: STOP MARKER written for token key <key> until <+30m> (30m)
  — `classifyHttp` read it as `ratelimit`. Every write by this token is refused until then.
```

A proxy path denial is not a rate limit. Waiting 30 minutes cannot clear it — the path is closed by policy, so the marker refuses writes for half an hour on a condition that will read exactly the same afterwards.

## The mechanism, read at source

`scripts/pm/label-write.mjs:310`:

```js
if ((status === 403 || status === 429) && Number(rateRemaining) === 0) return 'ratelimit';
```

The `ratelimit` arm is meant to fire on `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`. It instead fires whenever that header is ABSENT, because of how the callers spell absence and how `Number` coerces it. `scripts/pm/close-cards.mjs:459` and `:482` pass `null` for a missing header (`rateRemaining === null ? null : Number(rateRemaining)`), and `scripts/pm/fleet-token.mjs:461` passes `rateRemainingOf(headers)`.

Coercion, measured rather than recalled:

| value passed | `Number(v) === 0` |
|:--|:--|
| `undefined` | `false` |
| `null` | **`true`** |
| `''` | **`true`** |
| `'0'` | `true` |
| `'4321'` | `false` |

⇒ Every 403 that carries no rate-limit header — a proxy denial, an org policy denial, a `Bad credentials` — is classified `ratelimit`.

## The same repository already has the correct guard, twelve lines of intent away

`scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs:430` writes the very same test WITH the absent-vs-zero guard:

```js
if (remaining !== null && String(remaining).trim() !== '' && Number(remaining) === 0) …
```

And `write-pace.mjs` accepts `classifyHttp`'s verdict as an input rather than re-deriving it (`:426`, and its self-test at `:1391` pins that as deliberate: «`classifyHttp`'s own ratelimit verdict is accepted as an input, not re-derived»). So the correct guard in `write-pace` is bypassed by the incorrect one upstream.

## The intended rule is already written down, and this violates it

`scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs:1388`, a passing self-test assertion:

> `⛔ a plain 403 does NOT — that is about the credential, and waiting fixes nothing`

That test passes because it constructs its input directly. It cannot catch this, because the defect is in what `classifyHttp` hands `write-pace`, not in what `write-pace` does with it.

## Suggested shape of the fix, ⛔ not a ruling

Give `classifyHttp` the guard `write-pace.mjs:430` already has, so an ABSENT header is distinguished from a header reading zero. Per the repo's own failure-fixing order — delete the construction that permits the error before adding a check — the narrower option is worth weighing first: have the callers pass `undefined` rather than `null` for an absent header, which the truth table above shows already behaves correctly. Either way the regression pin is a 403 with no rate-limit header, asserting no marker is written.

## Blast radius

`classifyHttp` is exported from `label-write.mjs` and called by `close-cards.mjs` (`:403`, `:477`, `:597`, `:669`) and `fleet-token.mjs` (`:461`). Any of those meeting a 403 without the header writes the same unwarranted stop.

## Not in scope here

⛔ The proxy policy that produced the 403 is a separate matter and not this card's. ⛔ This card does not propose changing `write-pace`'s accept-the-verdict design, which its own self-test declares deliberate.
